summary: Intro discovery focused on unit economics for hosted vs dedicated Redwood deployments. Agreed next steps: pricing sheet, security docs, and a benchmark run with sample traffic.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Penumbra Head of Data), Priya Singh (Penumbra ML Eng), Javier Morales (Penumbra CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro from our side, i'm maya chen AE on Redwood, this is liam our se, we'll run through cost/unit econ and then dig into your traffic profile.
[00:28] Ethan: yeah thanks maya, appreciate it. Quick context, we run inference for quant trading signals, super latency sensitive for some routes, but bulk gen for research, budget is pretty tight, trying to understand hosted vs dedicated costs.
[01:03] Liam: got it. can I ask ballpark qps and token sizes? that drives batching and cost.
[01:30] Priya: typical inference call is 120 qps on average, spikes to 600 during open, tokens per request ~450 average, sometimes as high as 2k for longer traces.
[02:10] Javier: also, security is non-negotiable — need SOC2, VPC peering or private, and KMS for keys.
[02:40] Maya: noted. on pricing, our hosted API is per-token with volume tiers, and Dedicated is reserved capacity with effective unit cost reductions once you hit commit. main levers are batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization.
[03:12] Ethan: how much does batching actually move the needle? we worry about tail latency.
[03:40] Liam: batching reduces tokens per GPU cost; for your bursty profile we typically do dynamic batching with latency SLOs — you can set max latency to keep tail behavior. in our internal numbers, batching + prefix caching can drop per-token by ~30-60% depending on hit rate.
[04:15] Priya: prefix caching? do you mean KV cache? we've seen cache misses for diffs, and i worry about statefulness in multi-tenant hosted.
[04:42] Liam: yes KV cache, sometimes called prefix or KV, on Hosted we do tenant-isolated caching with TTLs; Dedicated gives more control and persistent cache across instances which increases hit rate for repeated prompts.
[05:10] Maya: and quantization — 8-bit/4-bit options, plus some model variants we recommend — can reduce inference cost 2x with minor quality tradeoffs for scoring pipelines.
[05:40] Ethan: interesting. can you give sample per-token numbers? rough is fine.
[06:05] Maya: sure rough hosted list price is $0.00006/token for long context gen at low volume (example), with committed dedicated you can get to effective $0.00002-$0.00003/token depending on commit and batch efficiency. those are illustrative — we'll share tailored pricing.
[06:45] Priya: that's a big spread. how do we model our mixed workload with both latency-critical and bulk?
[07:10] Liam: we advise hybrid routing: route low-latency routes to dedicated or reserved low-batch pools with smaller batch windows, and bulk jobs to high-batch pools or background jobs; smart routing gives best cost/perf.
[07:45] Javier: any caveats around throughput on Dedicated? like saturation, autoscale?
[08:10] Liam: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; you can reserve baseline and allow bursts to hosted fallbacks if overloaded. we expose queue depth and token throughput metrics in Console.
[08:40] Ethan: what about data retention and audit logs? we have compliance audits monthly.
[09:00] Maya: we offer audit logs, per-request tracing, and for Private/VPC deployments you control retention and your KMS; Hosted offers configurable retention windows and export hooks. SOC2 cert available, will send docs.
[09:30] Priya: ok good. for the benchmark, we want to run a 1M token synthetic run with our traffic shape. what does that look like operationally?
[09:55] Liam: we can run bench on Hosted or spin up a Dedicated trial node; we'll need your sample traffic CSV, seed prompts, and SLO targets. typical runbook: run baseline on your dataset, collect token counts, latency percentiles, and cache hit rates.
[10:30] Ethan: timeline? we want results within two weeks.
[10:50] Liam: doable — we'll schedule this week if you share traffic by Friday.
[11:15] Maya: price modeling: we'll build a unit-cost sheet modeling your qps, avg tokens, cache hit, batching window, and commit level; that'll show projected monthly spend across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[11:50] Priya: any hidden costs? storage for KV cache? network egress?
[12:12] Maya: KV cache storage negligible on Dedicated, on Hosted it is included in tier; network egress billed per cloud provider if cross region — we'll call that out. Premium support and long-term retention are add-ons.
[12:40] Ethan: competitors — we're also evaluating OpenAI and Bedrock; cost is a driver but so is latency.
[13:00] Maya: understood — we try to show unit economics side-by-side and run parity benchmarks.
[13:20] Javier: one more — can you lock latency SLOs in Dedicated contract?
[13:40] Maya: yes we offer SLA-backed latency and uptime targets for Dedicated with contractual terms depending on commit.
[14:05] Priya: transcriptions sometimes show Redwood product names wrong, is there a doc that maps names to features?
[14:20] Liam: yes we'll send a one-pager mapping: Serving runtime, KV cache, Smart routing, Redwood Console etc.
[14:40] Ethan: ok next steps recap please.
[14:50] Maya: recap: we'll send tailored pricing sheet + unit model, SOC2 and security pack, and a runbook to kick off the 1M-token benchmark. liam will run the bench and share metrics. penumbra to share traffic and SLOs.
[15:20] Priya: sounds good. a couple of technical clarifiers — does the KV cache persist across restarts in Dedicated?
[15:40] Liam: yes on Dedicated with local persistent cache and optional external cache store for long lived persistence; Hosted has TTL but is tenant isolated.
[16:00] Ethan: any immediate blockers on our side? we need cost estimates for Q2 budget review.
[16:20] Maya: we'll prioritize the pricing model and have a draft by Friday 2026-03-06.
[16:40] Javier: perfect. any mention of quantization regressions? we run evals on prompts for scoring — how invasive is 4-bit?
[17:00] Liam: usually minimal for scoring, we recommend running a small eval set to check quality delta. we'll include recommended quant profiles per model.
[17:30] Priya: do you support private deployments on prem for our air-gapped research cluster?
[17:50] Maya: yes Redwood Private supports on-prem air-gapped with customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integration, but that has different pricing and lead time.
[18:10] Ethan: okay, anything else?
[18:25] Maya: we'll send all artifacts; try to get traffic sample. thanks all.

[57:00] End recap and confirm next steps — call ends ~10:58 AM PT.
